description: Rootz Asylum Village at DEF CON 26 features community talks and discussions on hacking and security culture with 2 sessions.

talks.title: Day 2
talks.summary:
### Welcoming the Next Generation of Hackers
At 00:00, mentors and organizers open Day 2 of r00tz Asylum at DEF CON 26, welcoming young hackers, parents, and security educators to a full day of hands-on security workshops and interactive learning.

### Memory Safety, Buffer Overflows, and Modern Compilers
At 21:09, mentors break down low-level programming concepts. They explain how stack-based buffer overflows occur in compiled languages, demonstrating how modern compilers incorporate safeguards such as address space layout randomization (ASLR) and stack canaries to prevent memory exploitation.

### The Ethos and Heritage of Hacker Culture
At 41:48, the discussion explores the history and cultural traditions of the hacker community. Mentors contrast modern walled gardens with early computing eras of the 1980s, inspiring youth to embrace curious exploration, reverse engineering, and open knowledge sharing.

### Collaboration and Teamwork in Capture The Flag
At 01:02:44, the presentation emphasizes community and peer learning. Mentors encourage students to collaborate across workstations, share debugging insights, and work together on solving CTF challenge tracks rather than hacking in isolation.

### Web Application Vulnerabilities and the r00tz Honor Code
Concluding between 01:22:58 and 01:30:00, instructors demonstrate practical web application security testing using Burp Suite. They reinforce the foundational r00tz Asylum Honor Code, reminding young hackers that technical skills must always be applied ethically and constructively to protect systems and defend digital rights.
